comparator.name: BSc Data Science and Society
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026–2027 catalogue totals 180 EC: 60 EC of compulsory first-year work; 40 EC of common second-year work plus the 20-EC AI and Society specialisation; and a 60-EC third year comprising a 30-EC minor, 5 EC Advanced Programming, 5 EC Research Design and Project Management, a 15-EC Bachelor Thesis and 5 EC Human Machine Interaction. AI and Society is selected because it is the first-listed specialisation, independently of UCR fit. The catalogue's course records and term data assign 15 EC to the thesis and 5 EC to research design, resolving the inverse credit labels currently displayed on the public programme page.

routeSelection.basis: The generic target does not select between the official AI and Society and Cognitive Technology specialisations. AI and Society appears first on the official programme page and in the catalogue, so it is selected without reference to UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Data science, AI & society
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule visibly combines programming, data analysis, machine learning and AI with ethics, governance, sociology, law, communication, sustainability and applied research.
alternatives.concept: The closest UCR response integrates data-science and AI foundations with social research, governance, ethics, communication and organisational application. It mirrors the programme's technical-and-societal bridge while acknowledging missing dedicated human-rights, field-project and thesis sequences.
progression: Programming, mathematics, data, social science and research foundations precede machine learning, deep learning, AI decision systems, governance, ethics and advanced applied analysis. All prerequisites and offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Cognitive technology & human-data interaction
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines data and AI with cognition, perception, psycholinguistics, computer vision, social psychology, human–machine interaction and responsible communication.
alternatives.concept: This official-structure direction develops the programme's Cognitive Technology specialisation through programming, data science, machine learning, computer vision, cognition, perception, psycholinguistics and human-centred research.
progression: Programming, mathematics, psychology, neuroscience and research foundations precede machine learning, computer vision, higher cognition, human-centred AI, psycholinguistics and advanced research. All prerequisites and offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest route, this curriculum replaces more than four governance, sociology, business and policy courses with neuroscience, cognition, perception, psycholinguistics, computer vision, health psychology and media-production work.

blocks: Programming, data, statistics and machine learning
Introduction to Data Science provides closely aligned foundations but not the programme's full societal framing.
Introduction to Programming supplies Python and computational problem-solving foundations.
Machine Learning directly develops statistical and predictive modelling.
Probability & Statistics develops probability, estimation and inference.
Networks & Operating Systems provides systems context but not a full databases-and-datasources course.
Neural Networks & Deep Learning develops advanced analysis of large and complex data.
Sociology analyses institutions and social consequences but is not a dedicated science-and-technology-studies course.
Political Philosophy supplies concepts for legitimate governance and public responsibility.
Contemporary Social Theory examines trust, institutions and social repair around modern systems.
AI Ethics directly addresses fairness, privacy, responsibility and accountability.
Qualitative methods supports empirical analysis of social problems and data practices.
Strategy & Digital Transformation examines organisational adoption of data and digital technology.
Ethics supports evaluation of digital impacts on dignity, justice and responsibility.
Media & the Environment analyses visual rhetoric, public understanding and sustainability.
Peace & Conflict examines political governance and responsibility, but not specialist AI regulation.
AI skills, decisions and responsible systems
Decision-making in AI develops planning and behaviour under uncertainty.
Optimization Methods in AI develops search, constraints and optimisation.
Reinforcement Learning develops advanced learning algorithms.
Persuasive Communication addresses influence and ethics but not the full politics of AI.
Personal & Professional Development includes presenting evidence, though not specialist data visualisation.
Research Methods & Statistics develops research design, sampling and project work.
UCR has sustainability and governance courses, but none in these schedules reproduces the specialist component.
Groningen requires a 10-EC external-partner field project; no scheduled UCR course is an equivalent.
Groningen reserves 30 EC for a genuine minor; the UCR pathways are complete fixed examples.
The UCR sequence develops programming and advanced AI, but no separate scheduled course reproduces Advanced Programming.
Groningen requires a 15-EC thesis. UCR optional independent research is shown separately.
The cognitive UCR direction has relevant psychology and media, but no single course reproduces Human Machine Interaction.
No scheduled UCR course reproduces the dedicated Human Rights in the Digital Age I component.

selection.assessment: The closest route covers the selected AI and Society specialisation and the programme-wide technical, ethical, legal, organisational and societal bridge. The second official specialisation supports one clearly distinct cognitive-technology route. Remaining interests are already substantive parts of these two curricula rather than independent third pathway generators.

core: Programming, databases, statistics, visualisation and machine learning
Societal, ethical and human-rights consequences of datafication
Governance, law, policy and sustainability for data and AI
Applied data projects, organisations and public communication
Responsible AI methods, research design and professional practice
adjacent: Cognitive technology, computer vision, speech and human-data interaction
questions: How can data and AI address societal and organisational problems?
How should data systems be governed to protect dignity, privacy and fairness?
How can technical evidence be visualised and communicated for responsible decisions?

notes.text: Groningen combines a sustained technical data-science sequence with dedicated human-rights, innovation-governance, field-project, human–machine-interaction and 15-EC thesis components. UCR offers strong related liberal-arts pathways, but not that integrated professional sequence.

The current Ocasys 2026–2027 catalogue assigns 15 EC to the Bachelor Thesis and 5 EC to Research Design and Project Management. Those authoritative course records are used instead of the reversed credit labels on the general programme page.
